tagline: A specialty materials company focused on activated carbon production and renewable forestry investments
hero_kpi_rationale: The improvement in gross margin by 1.8% in 2025 versus a gross loss of -0.5% in 2024 (+2.3 points) reflects a significant operational turnaround following a reduction in unit production costs for activated carbon, indicating improved efficiency despite lower volumes and a restructuring context.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Money earned by the company through its core activities of selling activated carbon.
kpis.description: Revenue is primarily derived from the sale of activated carbon, supplemented by air filtration products. The decline is attributable to a reduction in sales volumes from 43,989 tons in 2024 to 31,237 tons in 2025.
kpis.signal: Significant decline in activated carbon sales due to volume reduction of 12,752 tons (29%).

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of goods sold, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin improved significantly, moving from a gross loss of $0.18 million in 2024 to a profit of $0.65 million in 2025, primarily driven by a decrease in activated carbon unit cost from $1,145 per ton to $1,118 per ton.
kpis.signal: Notable improvement in gross margin from -0.5% to +1.8% due to a 2.4% reduction in unit cost.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Profit achieved after operating expenses, before taxes and interest.
kpis.description: Operating loss of $10.98 million in 2025 versus $12.49 million in 2024 reflects substantial allowances for credit losses ($8.9 million), partially offset by reductions in G&A and R&D expenses.
kpis.signal: Operating margin strongly negative due to credit loss provisions and declining revenue.

kpis.name: R&D Expenses (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Portion of research and development expenses relative to total revenue.
kpis.description: R&D expenses dropped to $1,279 in 2025 versus $135,146 in 2024 following the termination of research and development programs in November 2023 as part of cost-cutting measures.
kpis.signal: Near-total halt in R&D investments since November 2023 as a cost-saving measure.

kpis.name: Allowance for Credit Losses
kpis.explanation: Accounting provisions for receivables deemed uncollectible or high-risk.
kpis.description: Allowances for credit losses amounted to $8.9 million, stable compared to $9.0 million in 2024. A significant provision of $18.2 million was recorded for an aged receivable, partially offset by reversals of $9.4 million on customer receivables and supplier advances.
kpis.signal: Stable but substantial provisions reflecting high credit risk, including an $18.2 million provision for aged receivables since September 2024.

kpis.name: Net Loss
kpis.explanation: Net financial loss after all expenses, taxes, and financial charges.
kpis.description: Net loss of $11.14 million in 2025 compared to $14.04 million in 2024 reflects improved profitability. Gains from disposal of subsidiaries ($0.82 million) and reduced G&A expenses partially offset declining revenue and credit loss provisions.
kpis.signal: Net loss reduced by 20.6% due to gains from subsidiary disposals and lower operating expenses.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €0.11 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt

risks.title: Risk of Nasdaq delisting and loss of liquidity
risks.summary: The company received a delisting notice from Nasdaq on January 16, 2026, as the closing price remained below $1.00 for 30 consecutive days. Ineligible for any additional compliance period due to two cumulative reverse splits (ratio 1:750). A delisting would result in: reduced liquidity, classification as a penny stock, limited analyst coverage, and impaired future financing capacity.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk listed first in the document (Item 3 Recent Developments). Highly intense language: « delist », « suspension of trading », « penny stock », « reduced liquidity ». Trend UP: two reverse splits (1:30 in 2024, 1:25 in 2025), delisting notice issued January 16, 2026, appeal pending. Critical impact on future financing ability.

risks.title: Dependence on Chinese regulation and VIE risk
risks.summary: The majority of operations are conducted in China through Variable Interest Entity (VIE) structures. The Chinese government may intervene, regulate foreign securities offerings, or require material operational changes. Specific risks include restrictions on PRC subsidiary dividends, foreign exchange controls, potential tax reclassification as a Chinese resident enterprise, and increased CAC oversight on cybersecurity and data.
risks.score_rationale: Major structural risk mentioned four times in Item 3 (« Risks Relating to Doing Business in the PRC »). Highly intense language: « significantly limit or completely hinder », « value of securities significantly decline or be worthless ». Majority of operations in China via VIE structure. Trend STABLE but categorical weight very high.

risks.title: Cybersecurity risk and data review by CAC
risks.summary: The Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) may require a cybersecurity review if the company collects personal data from over one million users or data affecting national security. Currently not subject to review, but risk is increasing if PATHENBOT (robotics/automation) or oil trading activities collect more user or sensitive operational data.
risks.score_rationale: PRC-specific risk explicitly mentioned in Item 3 with technical details (« Cyberspace Administration of China », 1 million user threshold). Language moderate but precise. Trend STABLE: currently not subject (<1M users), but emerging risk if expansion occurs. Medium categorical weight for tech/robotics sector.

risks.title: Concentration of shareholder control and governance risk
risks.summary: Ms. Yefang Zhang controls 86.4% of voting power through an irrevocable proxy granted by Weastfinace (631,391 Class B shares). This extreme concentration limits minority shareholder rights, creates risk of unilateral decisions (acquisitions, dilutive financings), and reduces governance protections.
risks.score_rationale: Major governance risk: Ms. Yefang Zhang controls 86.4% of voting power via irrevocable proxy agreement (September 2025). Positioned in Item 3 (Recent Developments). Clear language: « irrevocable proxy », « controls approximately 86.4% ». Trend UP: increased concentration via recent agreement. Impact on minorities and strategic decisions.

risks.title: Dependence on convertible debt financing and dilution
risks.summary: The company raised $13.9 million via three convertible notes from Streeterville Capital (7% interest, 12-24 month maturities). Each note includes a conversion floor (e.g., $0.626, $0.10412) that significantly dilutes existing shareholders. Risk of refinancing if stock price remains low, and cash pressure at maturity (January 2027-2028).
risks.score_rationale: Major capital risk: three convertible debt instruments issued in 2024-2026 (Streeterville: $7.51M in January 2026, $3.15M in October 2024, $3.23M in April 2025). Technical language: « convertible », « floor price », « original issue discount ». Trend UP: rapid accumulation of convertible debt. High dilutive impact on existing shareholders.

risks.title: Integration and operational risk of Blessing Logistics acquisition
risks.summary: The company signed a framework agreement to acquire 82% of Blessing Logistics Ltd. (Alberta, Canada), an oil trading company, for approximately $2 million in Class A shares. Risks include incomplete due diligence, complex operational integration (new oil sector), Canadian/energy regulatory risks, and shareholder dilution if the deal is finalized.
risks.score_rationale: Major acquisition risk announced January 25, 2026: acquisition of 82% of Blessing Logistics (Canadian oil trading) for ~$2M in shares. Moderate language: « framework agreement », « subject to change », « due diligence ». Trend NEW: very recent agreement, 60-day window for final deal. Medium categorical weight (business diversification).

risks.title: Non-core business diversification and strategic risk
risks.summary: The company operates through three unrelated business lines: (1) sale of materials/activated carbon in China (MZ Pintai, Yunnan Yuemu, Zhejiang New Material), (2) robotics/automation in North America (PATHENBOT), (3) oil trading in Canada (Blessing Logistics pending). Risks include lack of synergies, managerial dilution, and limited ability to create value in each segment.
risks.score_rationale: Strategic risk: highly fragmented portfolio (materials in China, robotics/automation in North America, oil trading in Canada). Language implicit: « holding company with no material operations of its own ». Trend UP: recent addition of Blessing Logistics. Medium categorical weight but impact on strategic focus.

risks.title: Liquidity risk and dependence on PRC subsidiary dividends
risks.summary: CN Energy is an offshore holding company (BVI) with no direct operations; it relies entirely on dividends and distributions from Chinese subsidiaries (MZ HK, PATHENBOT). Risks include PRC restrictions on capital repatriation, foreign exchange controls, limitations on intra-group loans, and inability to fund operations if subsidiaries do not pay dividends.
risks.score_rationale: PRC-specific liquidity risk: holding company with no operations, dependent on dividends from Chinese subsidiaries. Intense language: « materially adverse effect on our ability to conduct our business ». Trend STABLE but categorical weight very high for offshore structure. PRC restrictions on capital repatriation.

ai_positioning.summary: CN Energy does not mention any initiatives related to artificial intelligence in its financial or operational documents. The company focuses on activated carbon production and renewable forestry investments, with initiatives centered on traditional operational cost optimization.
evidence: No mention of AI, machine learning, or advanced automation in the 20-F and 6-K filings
R&D investments were halted in November 2023 as a cost-cutting measure
Strategic initiatives focus on unit production cost optimization and acquisition of operational subsidiaries
